introduction: “Though but few persons accepted and were converted in the Day of each one of the Manifestations, yet these few surpassed and overcame great multitudes.” The guide collects passages on the fewness of those who respond: the feast is spread and few come, the pearls lie without seekers, the believer is “rarer than red sulfur”; and with them, the assurance that recognition is a grace, that a few are worth more than a multitude, and that small beginnings grow. The Bible has the whole theme: the narrow gate, the sower, the excuses of the invited, the nine who did not return, the remnant, Elijah’s unsuspected seven thousand, Gideon’s three hundred, the mustard seed and the leaven. The Qur’an says “few of My bondmen are thankful” and “how many a little company hath overcome a mighty host”. Jesus’s remark that the harvest is plentiful and the labourers few turns the complaint around, and Henry V’s “happy few” shows how easily a small band’s consolation becomes its pride.
questions: “Many are called but few are chosen.” How does reading 2 understand the choosing? Is it something done to people or by them?
The readings say both that recognition is pure grace and that people “turned away”. Can both be held? How does the parable of the sower divide the responsibility?
Elijah believed he alone was left and was wrong by seven thousand. What does that story say to a community that counts its own small numbers?
“The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.” Would the readings agree that the scarcity is of workers and not of receptive souls?
What are the temptations of belonging to a “happy few”, and what in the readings guards against them?

outside.why: Few accepted each Manifestation, yet the few overcame multitudes. The Qur’an: how many a little company hath overcome a mighty host by Allah’s leave!
Gideon’s army is cut from thousands to a handful on purpose: by the three hundred men that lapped will I save you; and let all the other people go.
The reading interprets this verse: for many are called, but few are chosen.
Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
Recognition attained through His preceding mercy. Paul: there is a remnant according to the election of grace; and if by grace, then is it no more of works.
The sages cannot comprehend and the little children do. Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
Bats do not perceive the sun. He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
This fewness is better than that abundance. Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
A few violets in Baghdad were dearer than a garden full. Prince Hal: if all the year were playing holidays, to sport would be as tedious as to work; nothing pleaseth but rare accidents.
The kingdom is like a merchant who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

Of three hundred and fifty believers a handful remained, and the rest later returned. Elijah thought himself the only one left, and was told: yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal.

Many heard the call and turned away; many heard and were drawn. A sower went forth to sow, and the seed fell by the wayside, on stony places, among thorns, and into good ground. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.
The sea of bounty is surging, yet none attained but whom God willed. Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?
The feast has been sent down and none seeks it. In the parable of the great supper the invited all with one consent began to make excuse: a piece of ground, five yoke of oxen, a wife.
There are seekers for everything except the pearls of wisdom. The Qur’an’s aside: few of My bondmen are thankful.
None with hearing to hearken, save a few. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
Many listened to the glad tidings and remained unmoved. Ten were cleansed; one turned back to give thanks. Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?

What benefit, when those who would taste are few? Jesus sees the shortage on the other side: the harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few. Are receptive souls scarce, or those who go to find them?
When the Sun of Revelation dawned, all were veiled save a few. When the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
The reading turns on this verse: thy Lord brought forth the seed of the Children of Adam and made them testify: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yea, verily.

The hosts that render the Cause victorious are goodly deeds, and they are few. Abraham bargains for Sodom down to ten: I will not destroy it for ten’s sake. What does a small number of the righteous do for the many, in that story and in these readings?
The kingdom is like leaven hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
Discerning souls are few in every age. Thoreau: any man more right than his neighbors constitutes a majority of one already.
Small beginnings. The least of all seeds, which when it is grown is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree.
The prophet to those disheartened by a modest rebuilding: for who hath despised the day of small things?

The believer is rarer than red sulphur. Henry before Agincourt makes rarity a boast: we few, we happy few, we band of brothers; and gentlemen now abed shall think themselves accursed they were not here. The readings console a small community with its fewness. What keeps that consolation from becoming Henry’s pride?

Those steadfast in love are rarer than the elixir. Jesus over the city: how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Is the tone of the readings lament, warning or resignation?
The signs are manifest to all, and few respond. Ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise, not many mighty, not many noble, are called.

shortfall: Readings 10 to 23 say one thing in fourteen ways (the gift is abundant, the seekers few); the companions given to that stretch answer all of it and one fewer than the guide’s number was placed.

kings-seven-thousand-in-israel.text: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him

judges-by-the-three-hundred.text: And the Lord said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand: and let all the other people go every man unto his place

quran-few-are-thankful.text: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful.
